passage:
A piano was placed in the city park with a sign: "Play me."
Some people played beautiful music. Others only pressed a few keys. Children made noisy songs, and old people smiled as they listened.
One afternoon, a shy boy sat down and played a short piece. He made mistakes and stopped. A woman nearby clapped gently and said, "Please continue."
The boy tried again. This time, he finished.
The park piano was not there to find the best musician. It was there to give music a public place.
In a concert hall, people may worry about playing perfectly. In a park, music can simply belong to everyone.
